title: top-io.json — the module's top-level IO ports (authored, never derived)
description: The DUT boundary. derive-constraints renders create_clock / set_input_delay / set_output_delay / abstract_port from it; simulation-plan derives agents and transaction fields from it; each rtl-design child reads it for set_case_analysis. Authored by the specification stage's Wave 1; design.md §1.4.1 points here and carries no table. Two conditional requirements are expressed below rather than in Python: an output declares its owner, and a reset row declares polarity and kind.

name.description: The port name exactly as the netlist declares it, bit range included (e.g. token_in[4:0]). Emitted verbatim into get_ports / abstract_port, so it is not decomposed here.

width.description: Bit width. When name ends in a [h:l] range, check-coverage cross-checks width against it; an [i] index (a register-file element) carries no width claim and is skipped.

clock_domain.description: A clocks.json name. Clock and reset ports carry no IO delay; each data port gets set_input/output_delay against this domain.

interface_group.description: Groups ports into one TB agent / one vif.

owner.description: Required on an output: the manifest child that drives it, which must list this port in its frontmatter ports. Prefer a leaf child passed through the pure top over top-level glue.

encoding.description: A control or status port pins its bit/field-to-symbol meaning here, including the consumer obligation per code. Raw data / clock / reset ports have none. Enforced by the spec-review conformance lens, not by a deterministic gate.
